title: Smoked Salmon Strata With Rye and Crème Fraîche
description: In this playful riff on a bagel with cream cheese and lox, Food & Wine’s Justin Chapple makes a custardy rye bread pudding with capers, then tops it with smoked salmon and red onion. It’s warm, comforting and a guaranteed crowd-pleaser.
ingredients: 1 pound rustic rye bread with crust, cut into 1-inch (or smaller) pieces
1/4 cup drained capers, plus more for garnish
Thinly sliced smoked salmon and sliced red onion, for serving (maybe two of the little packages)
directions: In a large bowl, whisk the crème fraîche with the eggs, half-and-half, salt and pepper.
Add the bread, scallions and the 1/4 cup of capers and mix well.
Scrape into a 9-by-13-inch baking dish, cover with plastic wrap and let soak for 1 hour.
Bake the strata for 45 to 50 minutes, until puffed and the top is golden.
Scatter some salmon on top and garnish with red onion and capers. Serve, passing more salmon at the table.
notes:
Make Ahead:
The unbaked strata can be covered and refrigerated overnight. Bring to room temperature before baking.
